text.en: Why do families who share their fun and their troubles seem to be the happiest?

The poet praises families that stick together. Rich or poor, they find the finest mirth and hear the sweetest music because they share one another's joys and troubles. Brothers and sisters who go separate ways may shatter the charm of life.
The poem celebrates unity and the joint family. Its central idea is that love and sharing, not money, bring the real joys of earth.
Use the summary words brothers and sisters, joint family, bitterness and share their fun. Note the rhyming couplets and the cheerful tone.
